clue.text: It's sting could make Pegasus take to the air

definitions.text: It's sting could make Pegasus take to the air

parts.words: It's sting could make Pegasus take to the air
parts.note: Pegasus is the winged horse of myth; the insect's name reads as an instruction for a horse to go airborne

explanation.surface: A whimsical notion that a bite could launch the mythical winged horse skyward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's' is printed for 'Its'. Pegasus already flies, so the clue plays on the insect's name read as two words: a horse told to take wing.
explanation.definitionFit: This biting insect pesters livestock, especially equines, with a painful sting.

clue.text: Love is prized by oil producers

indicators.note: read as 'prised' open, the letters of these words are levered apart and rearranged

explanation.surface: Romance is treasured by the people who make oil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prized' signals the anagram of LOVE IS: think of something prised open.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressed fruit of the olive tree yields olive oil, so the trees' fruits are oil sources.

clue.text: A good man is a politician to make one's mark

parts.note: ST, short for saint, a good man
MP, Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A virtuous person enters politics to make a name for themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: To imprint or put a seal on something is to leave an impression on it.

clue.text: Frank gets a stove that is non-battery

parts.note: frank means open, free in speech
a range is a kitchen stove

explanation.surface: Someone candid acquires a cooker that doesn't run on batteries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'non-battery' looks electrical; it refers to hens not kept in battery cages.
explanation.definitionFit: Poultry allowed to roam outdoors are the opposite of birds kept in battery cages.

clue.text: The second person to' precede North German minor

parts.note: the second-person pronoun is you

explanation.surface: Grammar talk about pronouns ahead of a north German child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to'' is an OCR stray for 'to'; 'precede' just orders the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor is a person of lesser age, not yet an adult.

clue.text: Shrink from installing telephone in church

indicators.note: the church is pictured installing the phone, taking it within its letters

parts.note: CE, Church of England
to ring is to telephone

explanation.surface: Recoiling from having a phone put in at church.
explanation.definitionFit: To flinch or recoil in fear or embarrassment.

clue.text: Fratricide without the right to a memorial

indicators.note: used in its old sense of outside, so the brother-killer goes around the letter

parts.note: Cain killed his brother Abel in Genesis, the first fratricide

explanation.surface: A brother-killer denied the right to any monument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' seems to mean lacking, but here means outside: CAIN wraps around R.
explanation.definitionFit: A heap of stones raised as a landmark or monument to the dead.

clue.text: Fashionable fortune-teller gets a pound for opening the ceremony

parts.note: in means fashionable
an augur foretells the future
L, from libra, is the pound sign

explanation.surface: A trendy clairvoyant is paid a pound to start the event.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes a first event or speech that formally begins a term or institution.

clue.text: Taking a risk by strolling after midnight

indicators.note: places the walking word behind the letter taken from night

parts.note: the middle letter of the word night is G
strolling means ambling

explanation.surface: Being reckless by walking about late at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'midnight' is the middle of 'night', the letter G.
explanation.definitionFit: Betting or wagering is staking money on chance.

clue.text: Appearance indicates how old Violet is

parts.note: Vi is short for the name Violet
the contraction 's
age is how old one is

explanation.surface: A clue about telling a woman's age from her looks.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'how old Violet is' as Vi's age.
explanation.definitionFit: A face or countenance is one's outward look.

clue.text: As indignant as a weapons enthusiast!

explanation.surface: Someone angry likened to a gun lover.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means protesting angrily; literally it means bearing guns.

clue.text: It A golfer moved around quietly in childish game

indicators.note: the soft letter goes within the rearranged letters
the letters of these words are shifted into a new order

parts.note: P, piano, means quietly in music

explanation.surface: A golfer creeps about quietly in a kids' playground game.
explanation.walkthrough: The leading 'It' is an OCR stray. 'moved around' rearranges A GOLFER into LEAFROG; 'in' puts P inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A children's game in which players vault over each other's bent backs.

clue.text: Worry when child's horse falls into a river

indicators.note: the horse drops inside the river, so its letters go within

parts.note: the Nile is the African river
gee-gee, GG, is a child's word for a horse

explanation.surface: Anxiety when a toddler's pony tumbles into a river.
explanation.definitionFit: To nag or bother slightly, causing minor unease.

clue.text: Yankee supremo made allowance for everyone

parts.note: general means applying to all
to grant is to allow or concede

explanation.surface: A Northern commander being generous to all.
explanation.walkthrough: Ulysses S Grant led the Union (Yankee) army in the American Civil War.
explanation.definitionFit: Ulysses S Grant commanded the Union forces, the Northern side in the US Civil War.

clue.text: Perishing in Californian gold-rush?

explanation.surface: Dying during the rush for gold in California.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is slang for dying or being lost, and literally heading towards the Pacific as forty-niners did.

clue.text: Willingly permit land to be set aside

parts.note: lief is an old word meaning gladly or willingly
to permit is to allow

explanation.surface: Happily agreeing that a field should go unused.
explanation.definitionFit: Farmland left unplanted for a season rests uncultivated.

clue.text: Refuse to let the pages get dog-eared

definitions.text: to let the pages get dog-eared

explanation.surface: Declining to fold the corners of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: To reject an offer; literally to fold over page corners.

clue.text: Transaction enabling firm to get wood

parts.note: a firm is a business
deal is pine or fir timber

explanation.surface: A deal letting a company acquire timber.
explanation.walkthrough: DEAL is sawn softwood timber, pine or fir.
explanation.definitionFit: A commercial agreement or trade between parties.

clue.text: Spend it any way you will, Vicar!

definitions.text: Spend it any way you will, Vicar!

indicators.note: the letters can be arranged in whatever order you like

explanation.surface: Someone handing a clergyman his pay and telling him to use it freely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'any way you will' rearranges SPEND IT; the whole clue also describes a vicar's pay.
explanation.definitionFit: A fixed salary, especially one paid to a clergyman.

clue.text: Agree to give airman a little rope

parts.note: AC, aircraftman, an RAF rank
cord is thin rope

explanation.surface: Consenting to hand a pilot a bit of rope.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in harmony or concur.

clue.text: Retired judge takes good man on board

explanation.surface: An ex-judge welcomes a worthy fellow aboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Senior judges are given this honour; also the chess piece moving on the board.

clue.text: "One who steals my purse steals ." (Hamlet)

parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation: Iago's line that money stolen is worthless rubbish compared with good name

explanation.surface: A quotation with its last word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The line 'Who steals my purse steals trash' is actually Iago's in Othello, not Hamlet.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubbish, worthless stuff, as money is compared with reputation.

clue.text: One certain to be replaced immediately

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the letters are put back in a different order

explanation.surface: A single item sure to be swapped out right away.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom meaning in an instant, very quickly.

clue.text: Reprimands upset Home Counties seaman

indicators.note: in a down entry, upset turns the letters bottom to top

parts.note: SE, the South East of England, around London
a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: Telling-offs upset a sailor from the south of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns SETAR around. Home Counties are the counties surrounding London.
explanation.definitionFit: To rate someone is to scold them angrily.

clue.text: Mild manner gains regard

parts.note: mode is a manner or way
to rate is to regard or esteem

explanation.surface: A gentle approach earns respect.
explanation.definitionFit: Means not extreme, temperate.

clue.text: Admits to having given the lad permission

parts.note: let means allowed, given leave
a son is a lad

explanation.surface: Confesses to having allowed the boy to do it.
explanation.definitionFit: To reveal or disclose a secret.

clue.text: Pinch one's nose

explanation.surface: Squeezing your nostrils.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for to steal, and an old slang word for the nose.

clue.text: The disadvantage of a Catholic boarding school

explanation.surface: The drawback of a religious residential school.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawback; also Downside School, a Benedictine school in Somerset, England.
